headlines: MDC STUDENT NATHAN BENTLEY SHOT OUTSIDE NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE RESTAURANT

REMEMBERING NATHAN BENTLEY, RISING LOCAL STUDENT AND DEVOTED BROTHER
draft.article: Late Friday night, 18-year-old Miami Dade College student Nathan Bentley was fatally shot outside a McDonald's in northwest Miami-Dade. Earlier in the evening, Bentley and his mother, Nohely Bogert, attended a football game at a field directly across the street. Bentley, a recent Hallandale High School graduate known to loved ones as G Baby, enjoyed rapping and was an older brother to an 11-month-old sister and a 15-year-old brother. His mother shared that he was a role model who led by making good decisions. Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office detectives investigated the scene for roughly eight hours, gathering evidence including a bystander's cellphone. The shooter remains at large with no motive identified. Anyone with tips can call Miami-Dade Crime Stoppers at 305-471-8477.

draft.article:
South Florida is one of the premier spots in the country to celebrate Halloween this year, with Miami ranking sixth nationwide and Hialeah securing the 19th spot among 100 major U.S. cities evaluated.

Miami earned a total score of 57.73, bolstered by a sixth-place finish in Halloween fun due to its broad selection of activities and holiday businesses. The city also placed 31st for trick-or-treater friendliness and 32nd for weather.

Nearby Hialeah finished 19th with a 51.82 score. Hialeah ranked first in the nation for the most potential trick-or-treat stops and ninth for trick-or-treater friendliness, despite placing last for candy and chocolate stores per capita.

headlines: TWO INJURED AND ONE CHARGED AFTER HIALEAH APARTMENT GATHERING SHOOTING
VIOLENT HIALEAH GATHERING ENDS IN GUNFIRE AND CHARGES
STAND YOUR GROUND LAW APPLIED AFTER VIOLENT HIALEAH APARTMENT BRAWL
draft.article: A late-night gathering in Hialeah turned violent Friday around 11:46 p.m., leaving two men hospitalized after an altercation on the 6100 block of West 22nd Court. Hialeah police reported that 42-year-old Jonatan De Jesus Dzul Aguilar acted aggressively toward female guests inside a second-floor unit. When Idalberto Garcia Cardenas intervened, Aguilar hit him over the head with a ceramic vase. A physical struggle followed, during which Cardenas drew a firearm and Aguilar was shot in the face. Aguilar was airlifted to Jackson Memorial Hospital's Ryder Trauma Center and now faces an aggravated battery charge. Cardenas was treated at Palmetto General Hospital and will not face charges after detectives determined he acted in lawful self-defense under Florida's Stand Your Ground law.

items.desc: Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz says pulling security details was not retaliation against Miami-Dade’s mayor and commissioners after budget loss

headlines: SHERIFF TO END MIAMI-DADE MAYOR SECURITY DETAIL ON NOV. 6
MIAMI-DADE SHERIFF DENIES PAYBACK IN MAYOR SECURITY CUT
WHY MIAMI-DADE LEADERS ARE LOSING THEIR POLICE BODYGUARDS
draft.article: Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz is scheduled to pull deputies from protective security details for Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and county commissioners on Nov. 6. The move officially ends the longstanding sergeant-at-arms program that assigned plainclothes officers as drivers and bodyguards for local elected officials. In an Oct. 28 letter to Levine Cava, Cordero-Stutz insisted the change is based on operational priorities and resources, not retaliation for county budget reductions that left the agency with millions less than requested. Cordero-Stutz emphasized that deputies will continue addressing credible threats against anyone in the county, pointing to a marked squad car stationed outside the suburban residence of unpaid senior adviser Rabbi Mark Rosenberg following recent online threats.

More than 5,000 real estate and planning professionals gathered at the Miami Beach Convention Center for the 2026 Urban Land Institute Fall Meeting, putting our local growth pipeline in the national spotlight.

City leaders highlighted over $14 billion in citywide investments across hospitality, commercial, and residential sectors. On October 26, attendees toured North Beach, Surfside, and North Bay Village, concluding at 72 Park where Economic Development Director Steven Anthony and Lefferts CEO Mendy Chudaitov discussed North Beach revitalization efforts, including Ocean Terrace improvements and the Byron Carlyle Theater redevelopment.

Panels also covered workforce housing at The Anamar at Collins Park and major projects like the Grand Hyatt Miami Beach Convention Center Hotel.

items.desc: Erik Spoelstra has had similar Miami Heat moments before, coaching against a mentor in Stan Van Gundy and against a protege in David Fizdale. But Monday was different with Dusty May.

SOUTH FLORIDA COACHING ROOTS RUN DEEP
HOW A BOCA RATON CONNECTION SHAPED NBA HEAD COACHES
draft.article: Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra met a familiar South Florida peer on Monday night in Miami when the Mavericks defeated the Heat. Dallas head coach Dusty May, who previously led Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton from 2018 to 2024, shares an enduring bond with Spoelstra. Their relationship strengthened three years ago during Heat training camp on the FAU campus. Over the years, the 49-year-old May attended roughly 50 offseason practices and workouts with the Heat to study their methods. The connection extends to personnel as well. Spoelstra previously hired May's son Jack as a Heat video intern, and Miami currently rosters center Vlad Goldin on a two-way deal after Goldin played under May at both FAU and Michigan.
